record.text: Pt moved MICU to 4 Stepdown yesterday afternoon, extubated 2 days, on HFNC 40L/50%. I passed on what I had to the stepdown night RT at 1900. Pt plugged ~0230, sat 78%, rapid called, deep suction cleared it, back to ICU for obs. record.text:
Missed doses, pip/tazo, 3 East.
1) Team changed frequency q6h to q8h Tues ~1100 after creatinine improved.
2) EHR discontinues the old order and builds a new one. New one's first dose defaults to 'next standard admin time', which it set to Wed 0600, not Tues 1400.
3) MAR showed nothing due Tues afternoon or evening. RN had no reason to think anything was missing.
Pt went about 19 h without antibiotic. Found on my Wed AM profile review. Tmax 38.6 overnight, lactate normal, cultures redrawn. Second time I've seen the start-time default do this on a frequency change.

classification.label: TECH
classification.reasoning: The EHR discontinued the old order and defaulted the new order's first dose to 'next standard admin time' (Wed 0600 rather than Tues 1400), leaving the MAR showing nothing due, and the reporter notes this is the second time the start-time default has behaved this way on a frequency change.

record.text: Cross-cover, 0130. Paged for BP 196/108, pt with hx HTN, no symptoms. Typed 'hydr' into order search and clicked what I thought was hydralazine 10 mg IV. Recheck at 0230 still 190s and pt very drowsy, RN called me back, that's when we saw it. Gave hydralazine, BP came down. Sleepy till morning, otherwise fine. I'd been up since 0700 the day before, for what that's worth.

record.text: 4 mo with bronchiolitis on HFNC 8L/40%. About 0400 I came in to check on him and he was dusky, sat 79% on the monitor, no alarm - it was silenced. Mom was asleep in the chair. She told us after she'd been hitting silence all night because it kept going off in the high 80s and waking him up. The monitor lets anyone press it, stays quiet 2 min, then she'd press it again. Suctioned, went up to 10L/50%, 94% within a few min. Don't know if one of us showed her that button at some point or if she just figured it out.

record.text: Paged 1015 by day RN, new L facial droop + dysarthria, stroke alert called. Day RN had been in the room at 0800 and thought his speech was baseline - she'd never met him before today. Talking to night RN by phone afterward: around 0500 she noticed he was 'a little slurry,' figured it was the trazodone, meant to bring it up. Didn't make it into her note or into report at 0700, and nobody paged cross-cover. So LKW ends up ~0430, not this morning, and he's out of window. MRI pending. I'm not trying to hang this on one person, just laying out the times as best I have them.

record.text: Add-on lap appy, came down to pre-op while the rooms were turning over from the late-morning cases. Allergy field said NKDA, carried forward from a 2023 encounter. Pre-op checklist has 'allergies reviewed with pt' checked off by the RN. She'd had midazolam 2 mg from the standing pre-op order by the time I got to her and was pretty drowsy, so I went off the chart. Cefazolin at incision, then urticaria, wheeze, BP into the 70s. Epi x2, stabilized, case went ahead. Afterward her husband told us penicillin anaphylaxis in 2024 at an outside hospital. Not clear to me whether she was ever actually asked, or asked after she was already sedated.

record.text: Outpatient HD. Chairs 7 and 8 are about 3 ft apart, same machine model, same alarm tone. I had 4 chairs this shift. Heard a venous pressure alarm, went to 8, and 8's screen had an alarm up from a minute earlier, so I cleared it and reset. The one going off was actually 7. Chair 7's venous needle had pulled partway out under her blanket, EBL maybe 150-200 mL, pt dizzy, BP 88/50. NS bolus, needle replaced, nephrologist saw her before she left. I was facing 8 the whole time. From where I was standing I'm honestly not sure 7's screen was even visible.

classification.label: TECH
classification.reasoning: Two adjacent machines of the same model with the same alarm tone gave no way to localize the alarm, and a stale alarm still displayed on chair 8's screen falsely confirmed the wrong station.

record.text: 0705, rm 11, day +9 allo transplant, 1 unit PRBC, irradiated product required. Night RN had picked the unit up from blood bank before report. I scanned band and bag at the bedside - green check - and spiked it. She was going to come back in and read the tag with me before I started, but 14 was vomiting and she was still trying to finish report on her others. The scan had already come back good, so in my head the matching was done, and I started at 50 mL/h. She came in at 0725 and read the tag: no irradiation sticker. About 15 mL in. Stopped, BB notified, heme aware, workup per protocol, pt afebrile and stable. The scanner matches pt to unit. It doesn't know about special requirements.

classification.label: TECH
classification.reasoning: The bedside scanner returned a green check that confirmed only patient-to-unit matching, and the reporting RN states the check made the verification feel complete in their head, so the missing irradiation attribute was not surfaced by the technology before the transfusion started.
